blocks.x: Site twin with IoT energy orchestration, diesel runtime down 34% and site-visit costs down 28% across 6,800 domains
Identity withheld, a domain company whose margin lived or died with diesel and whose site visits were the second bill. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline quarter metered the truth: 61% of site energy from diesel where grid existed but was untrusted, generator runs scheduled by timer rather than battery state, and site visits triggered by alarms that arrived after the fault had cost money.
Site hardware was heterogeneous, three generator generations, four battery chemistries, and no twin existed that could decide anything. Energy data arrived monthly, reconciled by spreadsheet.

We built the site twin at scale: per-site energy model joining grid telemetry, battery health, generator hours and fuel levels, orchestration policies per hardware generation with the twin deciding charge and run schedules at the edge, fuel-theft and consumption anomalies detected as structures, and maintenance dispatched on predicted need. The timer retired; the twin works nights.
